samples.summary: Top-level `htmlLabels: false` may not actually turn off HTML labels — mermaid resolves it with `||` against the per-diagram default `true`
samples.evidence: mermaid.ts:470-477 asserts "the engine resolves labels through `config.htmlLabels ?? config.flowchart?.htmlLabels ?? true`". In mermaid 11 the label helper (rendering-util/rendering-elements/shapes/util.ts `labelHelper`, and createLabel.js) reads `node.useHtmlLabels || getConfig()?.htmlLabels || getConfig()?.flowchart?.htmlLabels` — a logical OR, not `??`. With OR, a top-level `false` is falsy and falls straight through to `flowchart.htmlLabels`, whose schema default is `true`, so the foreignObject label subtree is still built and the `` in a label is still fetched during layout. Additionally, other diagram types read their own namespaced keys (`class.htmlLabels`, `state.htmlLabels`, mindmap/er label paths) which the top-level key does not reach at all, so even under the `??` reading the mitigation is only partial. If either holds, the whole change is a no-op for the behavior it claims to fix. mermaid is not installed in this working tree so I could not read the installed 11.16.0 source to confirm; the config would need `flowchart: { htmlLabels: false }` (and the equivalent per-diagram keys) in addition to the root key.

samples.summary: Fixpoint strip loop is quadratic in fence length on untrusted input, with no size bound before it runs — a hostile note can hang the reader's tab
samples.evidence:
stripConfigDirectives() now loops until a fixpoint (lines 250-255). Each iteration runs an unanchored global `DIRECTIVE_RE` scan plus a full string copy over the whole remaining source, while `FRONTMATTER_RE` removes at most ONE leading block per iteration. A source of stacked ~10-byte `---
x
---
` blocks therefore costs O(n²/10): the docstring's own numbers (29 ms at 50 kB) only hold because it assumes mermaid's `maxTextSize` default bounds the input, but `maxTextSize` is enforced inside `mermaid.render()` (line 504) — strictly AFTER stripConfigDirectives() has already run on the raw fence body, which nothing in preview.ts or mermaid.ts caps. A 1 MB fence of stacked blocks is ~100k iterations over ~500 kB average, i.e. tens of GB of scanning/copying on the main thread, synchronously inside renderPass. Cross-carrier promotion (directive+frontmatter alternation) reaches the same iteration count. A cheap fix: bail out (or fall back to leaving the source intact / erroring the block) past a small iteration count or an input-length cap, since the docstring itself notes only a hostile fence stacks more than one carrier.

samples.summary: New test mutates the real mermaid singleton's global config and nothing resets it, so later cases in the process see a config this test installed
samples.evidence: preview.test.ts:639-645 imports the real `mermaid` module and calls `mermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false, securityLevel: 'strict', htmlLabels: false })`. mermaid's siteConfig is a process-global; `resetMermaidStateForTests()` (mermaid.ts:548-554) only clears this module's memos (`loaded`, `purifier`, `initializedTheme`, cache) and cannot undo it. Any later case that reaches the real engine — or any assertion about mermaid's default config — is now order-dependent. Note also this initialize omits `secure: SECURE_KEYS`, i.e. it installs a weaker global config than production. Secondary risk on the same line: `mermaid.mermaidAPI` is deprecated upstream; if it is dropped in a future 11.x the expression throws TypeError rather than failing the assertion meaningfully (`mermaid.getConfig()` would be the stable read).

samples.summary: No test verifies that htmlLabels actually changes label rendering; the 'engine actually honors it' case only reads the config back
samples.evidence: The test named 'sets an htmlLabels key the real engine actually honors' asserts only `mermaid.mermaidAPI.getConfig().htmlLabels === false`. mermaid's `assignWithDepth` merge stores arbitrary top-level keys, so this assertion passes even if no renderer ever consults the key (see the `||` fallback concern above) — exactly the failure mode the comment claims it guards against. Nothing in the suite exercises the label-resolution path (real mermaid cannot render under jsdom), so the mitigation is unverified end to end; a browser-lane case asserting a labelled node produces no `` (or no network request for `A[""]`) is what would actually cover it.

samples.summary: Fixpoint stripping now deletes diagram content mermaid itself would render, because the engine only does one pass
samples.evidence: mermaid extracts front matter once and then removes directives once; it never re-examines the text for a newly-leading `---` block. The loop at mermaid.ts:251-255 does, so a fence whose legitimate body happens to begin with a `---`-delimited block after the first strip (or whose body starts with `---` at all) has that content silently deleted before `mermaid.render()` sees it — a rendering difference/data loss relative to the engine, in the direction of over-stripping. Low impact and arguably the intended trade, but the docstring frames the loop as matching what the engine reads, which it does not; a note author sees content vanish with no error label.

finding.evidence: mermaid.ts:470-477 asserts "the engine resolves labels through `config.htmlLabels ?? config.flowchart?.htmlLabels ?? true`". In mermaid 11 the label helper (rendering-util/rendering-elements/shapes/util.ts `labelHelper`, and createLabel.js) reads `node.useHtmlLabels || getConfig()?.htmlLabels || getConfig()?.flowchart?.htmlLabels` — a logical OR, not `??`. Additionally, other diagram types read their own namespaced keys (`class.htmlLabels`, `state.htmlLabels`, mindmap/er label paths) which the top-level key does not reach at all, so even under the `??` reading the mitigation is only partial. If either holds, the whole change is a no-op for the behavior it claims to fix. mermaid is not installed in this working tree so I could not read the installed 11.16.0 source to confirm; the config would need `flowchart: { htmlLabels: false }` (and the equivalent per-diagram keys) in addition to the root key.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: mermaid.ts:473-479 passes only the top-level `htmlLabels: false` to `mermaid.initialize()`, with no `flowchart.htmlLabels` or per-diagram (`class`/`state`) equivalents, and the comment at mermaid.ts:470-472 asserts the engine resolves via `config.htmlLabels ?? config.flowchart?.htmlLabels ?? true`. So `not-present` fails. No downstream guard neutralizes it either: the module's own SECURITY note (mermaid.ts:41-49) and docs/design/notes/notes.md:506-510 state that `sanitizeSvg()` runs strictly after the engine lays the diagram out in the live document and "is not a fetch boundary", and `securityLevel: 'strict'` + `secure: SECURE_KEYS` (mermaid.ts:192) only stop a note from overriding the key, not the engine's resolution of it — so `already-guarded` fails. The decisive fact — whether mermaid 11's labelHelper/createLabel resolves with `||` (falling through a falsy top-level `false` to `flowchart.htmlLabels`, schema default true) or with `??` — cannot be checked here: there is no node_modules in this tree and mermaid is only a declared dependency (packages/notes/package.json:67). The repo's own tests do not close the gap: preview.test.ts:631-646 asserts only that `getConfig().htmlLabels === false` (config round-trip), and its comment concedes real mermaid cannot render under jsdom, while preview.test.ts:626-628 uses a stub engine and only checks what is asked for. If the reviewer's reading holds, the entire mitigation for the label-beacon issue is a no-op — a major behavioral defect in the correctness lane (wrong assumption about a resolution condition, broken invariant). Unverifiable either way from this repository, so the finding stays.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate on every checkable point. mermaid.ts:249-256 is an uncapped `for(;;)` fixpoint loop; FRONTMATTER_RE (line 222) is `^`-anchored and non-global so it strips at most one leading block per iteration, while DIRECTIVE_RE (line 221) is a global scan re-run over the whole remainder each iteration plus a full string copy — quadratic in the number of stacked carriers. The ordering claim also holds: the strip runs as the argument expression at line 504, before `mermaid.render()`, so mermaid's `maxTextSize` (only pinned as a name in SECURE_KEYS, line 183) cannot bound the input. I found no upstream cap: the sole call path is NotePreview.render (preview.ts:198-211) -> renderMermaidBlocks -> renderPass, with the fence body taken verbatim from the markdown-it token at preview.ts:76-78, and a repo-wide grep for content/size limits in packages/notes turned up only MAX_DISPLAY_NAME_LENGTH (display-name.ts:20). renderCache (mermaid.ts:111) only helps after the computation, and each keystroke produces a fresh uncached source. Note content is untrusted by the module's own SECURITY note (lines 18-21), so an unbounded synchronous main-thread loop is reachable on a real path; no guard makes it unreachable and it is a missing-bound runtime-correctness defect, not merely a style or design concern.
